title: [finding] AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails table names `content/docs/guides/` — the directory does not exist on main
body:
## Observation

AGENTS.md's Documentation Guardrails table carries the row:

| Path | Type | Rule |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `content/docs/guides/` | hand-written | Update `meta.json` when adding pages. |

but `content/docs/` on current `main` (`93304c2`) contains no `guides/` directory at all (top-level dirs: `ai`, `api`, `automation`, `capabilities`, `concepts`, `data-modeling`, `deployment`, `getting-started`, `kernel`, `permissions`, `plugins`, `protocol`, `references`, `releases`, `ui`).

Noticed while exercising #9866's provenance recompute: a temp page write to `content/docs/guides/…` failed with "No such file or directory" because the table row pointed at a directory that is not there.

## Why it matters (mildly)

The table is the reader's map of which docs trees are hand-written vs generated vs release-owned. A row naming a missing directory is the same drift class the docs-audit gate exists to catch in `ALL_HANDWRITTEN` (#4851) — here it is prose, so nothing checks it. The `meta.json` advice the row carries is real and applies to the trees that DO exist; it is anchored to a ghost path.

## Suggested disposition

Either drop the row or rename it to the tree(s) that took over guide content (e.g. `getting-started/` / `capabilities/`). AGENTS.md is a governed surface — the fix is a small governed PR, human merge.

Observation-class: filed unassigned, `finding` label, no `pm:queue`, per triage discipline.
